textbook: Clean cutaway textbook illustration of a SINGLE human osteocyte, a small star-shaped (stellate) bone cell, centered in a square 1:1 1080x1080 frame with lots of negative space around structures for later labels. The neutral dark charcoal background of the illustration itself must extend and touch all four edges of the canvas, filling it completely corner-to-corner. Do NOT place any border line, rectangle outline, frame, mat, margin, vignette or letterbox bar around the artwork — there must be NO visible edge or seam between a bordered inner picture and an outer margin; the picture IS the full canvas with zero uniform-colour margin at any edge. Match the exact house look of a refined educational plate: a MUTED, slightly desaturated palette (soft dusty tints, never bright primary or cartoon colours), THIN clean outlines (not heavy black strokes), gentle soft shading, each structure its own distinct soft colour fill. The cell body is small, flattened and star-shaped, sitting centered inside a pale ellipsoidal cavity (a lacuna) carved into a denser, richly textured band of mineralised bone matrix that fills the rest of the frame around it. Dozens of long, thin, branching dendritic processes radiate outward from the cell body in all directions, each process running cleanly through its own narrow tunnel (a canaliculus) drawn through the surrounding matrix — the processes must stay inside their canaliculi, never floating in open space, and a few processes should visibly touch neighbouring (mostly cropped-off) cells or their canaliculi at the frame edges to suggest the network. A neat quarter cut-away through the cell body reveals the interior: a single round-to-oval central nucleus, a modest amount of folded rough endoplasmic reticulum near the nucleus with tiny ribosome dots, a small Golgi stack, a few small oval mitochondria with faint inner cristae dispersed in the cytoplasm, and a very thin pale halo of pericellular fluid drawn as a fine gap between the cell membrane/processes and the wall of the lacuna and canaliculi. Anatomically faithful single human bone cell. Do NOT draw a cell wall, nucleoid, plasmids, multiple nuclei, a plump cuboidal cell sitting free on a bone surface (that is the earlier osteoblast stage), or a round smooth-surfaced cell without processes; this is NOT a bacterium and NOT a red blood cell. Absolutely NO text, letters, numbers, labels, scale bars, arrows, or watermarks in the image.
